title: TS2Python wire (proto 1) — bar
description: Payload emitted by EL_PublishBar: a complete OHLC bar at the interval named in `tf`. Frame 2 of a 2-frame ZMQ message; frame 1 is the UTF-8 symbol topic. Carries no bid/ask — InsideBid/InsideAsk are live-quote functions, not bar fields, and a quote pinned to a whole bar belongs only to its last print. See wire.md and semantics.md — schema validation alone is NOT sufficient to implement a correct binding.

proto.description: Protocol version. Named `proto` rather than `v` on purpose: the superseded wire used `v` and counted up to 4, so restarting at 1 under the same key would make {"v":1} a legal opening for both protocols — and the superseded v1 bar used kind "bar_1m", which a new binding would skip silently. A binding must refuse any frame where this key is absent or not 1. See wire.md.

tf.description: Interval this bar covers. Same vocabulary the storage layer partitions on, deliberately: a binding that cannot place a tf must refuse the frame rather than file it under a default, or one interval's bars end up in another interval's partition where nothing can distinguish them. Bucket alignment differs per interval — see semantics.md §2.2.

seq.description: Per-symbol monotonic sequence, shared with tick on the same symbol — both interleave on one topic, so one counter is what detects loss on that stream. Emitted as an unsigned 64-bit integer. See semantics.md §6.

sid.description: Publisher session id — the UTC epoch MICROsecond stamped at init. Compare for equality only; never read it as a timestamp.

ts.description: DLL receive-side wall clock, UTC epoch seconds. Latency measurement only. Must NOT be used for bucket alignment.

ts_str.description: Raw EL timestamp, yyyy-MM/dd-HH:mm:ss (24-hour). AUTHORITATIVE source for bucket_start: parse as America/New_York, convert to UTC. It is the bar's CLOSE time (EasyLanguage's Time), so a binding must subtract one tf before aligning to get the left label — see semantics.md §2. Not JSON-escaped, and not validated by the publisher.

el_volume.description: EasyLanguage's `Volume` reserved word, VERBATIM. On an intraday bar this is up-tick share volume alone — NOT the traded quantity, despite the name. On tf 1d it is total shares. The publisher deliberately performs no selection or conversion; the el_ prefix is there so a reader looks the word up instead of assuming. Meaningless for index/breadth symbols. See semantics.md §3.4.

el_ticks.description: EasyLanguage's `Ticks` reserved word, VERBATIM. On an intraday bar this is TOTAL share volume; on tf 1d it is a count of ticks (though measured daily data in this repo shows it byte-identical to el_volume, so treat the daily count as unconfirmed). This is the inverse of el_volume, which is exactly why both are shipped. See semantics.md §3.4.

el_upticks.description: EasyLanguage's `UpTicks` reserved word, VERBATIM. Intraday: up-tick share volume. Daily: total shares.

el_downticks.description: EasyLanguage's `DownTicks` reserved word, VERBATIM. Intraday: down-tick share volume. Daily: 0.

el_open_interest.description: EasyLanguage's `OpenInt` reserved word, VERBATIM. Always 0 for stocks and ETFs; meaningful only for futures and options.
